themes_detail.label: Park Rules Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violations spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week (1500% increase, z-score 8.66), suggesting a sudden deterioration in park conditions or enforcement in East Harlem parks over the past 7 days.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 8.66 indicates statistical anomaly at highest severity level
Spike is most recent and sharpest among all tracked violations
reporting_angles: What specific rule violations are occurring in East Harlem parks (Marcus Garvey, Jefferson, East River Waterfront)? Interview parks enforcement officers and residents.
Is this spike tied to a specific incident, facility closure, or enforcement gap? Check NYC Parks incident reports.

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs in Neighborhoods
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 4 reports LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.5 per week (700% increase, z-score 3.5), indicating a sharp uptick in dogs off-leash across East Harlem residential areas.
evidence: 4 unleashed dog complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 3.5 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Spike appears recent and sustained vs. longer-term baseline
reporting_angles: Interview residents about specific locations where unleashed dogs are congregating and whether any incidents (bites, confrontations) have occurred.
Check with NYPD Animal Care and Control on enforcement activity and whether staffing or summer season explains the uptick.

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints nearly doubled to 24 reports LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 12.4 per week (94% increase, z-score 3.26), suggesting new or expanded commercial activity, construction, or venues generating disturbance in East Harlem.
evidence: 24 commercial noise complaints last week vs. 12.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 3.26 indicates statistically significant spike
Commercial noise is a distinct subset from broader 1897 residential noise complaints, suggesting targeted source
reporting_angles: Identify which commercial venues or construction sites are generating complaints. Cross-reference 311 complaint addresses with DOB permits (578 filings recorded).
Interview affected residents on specific blocks (125th Street corridor is active per ULURP applications) about noise sources and impact on sleep/business.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Hot Spot
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints spiked to 10 reports TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 2.4 per week (321% increase, z-score 3.82), signaling either a new dumping site or cleanup enforcement gap in East Harlem.
evidence: 10 illegal dumping complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 3.82 indicates high statistical significance
Community Board budget requests include repeated requests for 'Increase Graffiti Removal/Cleaning' to Department of Sanitation, suggesting long-running sanitation concerns now sharpening
reporting_angles: Map the 10 illegal dumping complaints to identify geographic clusters. Are they on the same block or scattered across the district?
Interview DSNY on enforcement and cleanup response times. Cross-reference with 752 unsanitary condition complaints to see if they cluster in same areas.

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance and facility complaints surged to 21 reports TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 7.6 per week (175% increase, z-score 3.46), indicating deteriorating building or public infrastructure conditions across East Harlem.
evidence: 21 maintenance/facility complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 7.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 3.46 indicates statistically significant spike
Complements long-standing CB budget requests for 'park, building, or access improvements' and 'street lights,' suggesting persistent infrastructure neglect now acute
reporting_angles: Classify the 21 maintenance complaints: are they NYCHA buildings, street infrastructure, parks, schools, or transit? Identify which agency owns most complaints.
Interview residents on delayed repairs and ask which facilities have been waiting longest for fixes. Connect to broader affordability and habitability issues.
